evidence: app/package.json:13-15 — vite ^8.3.5, typescript ^7.0.2: exactly the current stable lines (Vite 8.3.5 released 2026-10-21 per vitejs/vite CHANGELOG; create-vite now templates TS 7)
app/src/api.ts:12 — import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL, still the current Vite env mechanism in Vite 8
app/tsconfig.json:2-13 — moduleResolution 'bundler', isolatedModules, strict: the current recommended shape for a Vite TS app, no legacy flags
app/package.json:9 — build is 'tsc --noEmit && vite build', no stale config files or hand-copied scaffolding that a newer release would emit differently
latest_apis.rationale: Toolchain and config are exactly the current stable generation (verified against Vite's Oct 2026 release notes), with no legacy-era patterns anywhere; there is almost no framework surface to misuse and what exists is used correctly.

evidence: app/src/main.ts:19-27,86-97 — hand-rolled RegExp routing + click interception where URLPattern (Baseline newly available since Sept 2025, in Chrome since 95, per MDN/web.dev) is now the platform answer
app/src/api.ts:113-120 — client fetch has no AbortSignal/timeout, unlike the server which uses AbortSignal.timeout(3000) at app/server.mjs:47
app/src/pages/home.ts:40 — inline 'pokemon.url.match(/\/(\d+)\/?$/)' instead of parsing with new URL(url).pathname
app/src/dom.ts:38 — replaceChildren (platform) used rather than innerHTML or a hand-rolled clear loop
app/src/format.ts:31 — findLast (ES2023) for latest English flavor text; app/src/pages/move.ts:14 — replaceAll
app/src/components.ts:57 — width/height + loading='lazy' + decoding='async' on sprites; app/src/style.css:374 — aspect-ratio
platform.rationale: Platform-first in nearly all cases (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, AbortSignal.timeout, replaceChildren, findLast, native dialog-less routing with history API), but the router is a hand-rolled regex now that URLPattern is Baseline, and client fetches lack any abort/timeout the platform provides for free.

evidence: app/package.json:13-15 — only devDependencies: typescript ^7.0.2 and vite ^8.3.5; zero runtime dependencies
app/server.mjs:1-6 — production server is 65 lines of node:http/node:fs/promises instead of express/sirv/servor
app/src/dom.ts:1-45 — 45-line h()/append() helper rather than a virtual-DOM or hyperscript package
app/src/style.css:1-4 — hand-written CSS with custom properties, no CSS framework (per spec)
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: no runtime deps at all, both devDeps are the current stable majors, and every place a package could have been pulled in (static server, DOM builder, styling) the platform/platform-adjacent choice was made instead.

evidence: app/src/main.ts:19-27 vs app/server.mjs:36-42 — route patterns duplicated across client and server (two runtimes, two regex lists); a route change touches both
app/src/api.ts:33-103 — all API access and response types behind one module; every page imports from here, so API-shape changes are localized
app/src/api.ts:11-14 + app/server.mjs:24-26 — API origin resolved in exactly one client module, injected at serve time so an environment change needs no rebuild
app/src/url-state.ts:1-21 — URL/history state changes isolated in one tiny module
app/src/pages/home.ts:32-52 — cross-resource type/generation maps derived inline inside the page module rather than the api data layer
app/src/main.ts:55-60 — navigation guarded by a monotonic token, so no reliance on framework internals or ordering; app/src/api.ts:107-109 — in-memory cache with failed requests evicted
churn_resistance.rationale: Boundaries are excellent (typed API layer, single config point, isolated URL state), so most upgrades would touch few files; the main ripple risk is the client/server route-pattern duplication and page-local data derivation in home.ts.

findings.issue: Route regexes and resource names are duplicated from app/src/main.ts:19-27; the two lists will drift when routes change (server is plain .mjs, client is TS).
findings.suggestion: Share one source of truth — e.g. a plain routes.mjs/JSON (pathname pattern + API resource) imported by server.mjs and by a thin TS wrapper, or have the server proxy unknown paths to the API once and cache the verdict.

findings.issue: Every HTML request performs an uncached upstream API round trip (3s timeout) just to pick 200 vs 404, adding latency to every navigation and a self-inflicted dependency on API uptime for the HTML shell.
findings.suggestion: Cache the per-pathname status verdict (or per resource/name pair) in a small Map with TTL, and fall back to serving 200 immediately when the API is slow rather than blocking the shell.

findings.issue: Client fetches have no timeout or abort; a hung API response leaves the page stuck on 'Loading…' indefinitely (the render timeout at main.ts:46 only shows text, never cancels).
findings.suggestion: Pass { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) } like the server does, and surface the failure through the existing errorPage().

findings.issue: Hand-rolled RegExp router; URLPattern has been Baseline newly available since Sept 2025 (Chrome since 95) and is the platform API for exactly this pattern matching.
findings.suggestion: Use new URLPattern({ pathname: '/pokemon/:name' }) for the route table — declarative, extracts named groups, and one construct shared with server.mjs's RESOURCE_ROUTES.

findings.issue: Cross-resource maps (pokemon types, species generation) are derived inline in the page module; other pages get the same kind of data through the api.ts layer.
findings.suggestion: Move these derivations into api.ts (e.g. pokemonTypeMap(), speciesGenerationMap()) so API-shape changes stay in one module and home.ts is pure view logic.

findings.issue: Duplicated ID-from-URL regex (Number(pokemon.url.match(/\/(\d+)\/?$/))) instead of the existing idFromUrl helper in format.ts:19 used elsewhere.
findings.suggestion: Import idFromUrl from ../format like components.ts:5 already does.

findings.issue: history.scrollRestoration = 'auto' is a no-op — 'auto' is already the default value.
findings.suggestion: Delete the line, or set it to 'manual' only if custom scroll restoration is actually wanted.

findings.issue: API base URL resolution spans a window global (__API_BASE_URL__) plus import.meta.env fallback; workable but the declare global Window augmentation is an unusual config seam for a Vite app.
findings.suggestion: Keep it (runtime injection is a sound choice) but consider a JSON script tag parsed in api.ts so the contract is data rather than a typed window property.

summary: A lean, current-generation vanilla Vite+TS app: Vite 8.3 and TypeScript 7 (both verified current), zero runtime dependencies, and clean module boundaries that would survive framework churn well. The main forward-looking weaknesses are client/server route-pattern duplication with an uncached upstream 404 probe on every HTML request, and a few spots (regex router, no client fetch timeout) where the platform now offers a better primitive. I'd merge with the two medium findings addressed.
